newsitem.title: UK: Britain, Egypt concerned over Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Britain, Egypt concerned over Mideast peace.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Britain and Egypt expressed grave concern on Thursday about the faltering Middle East peace process.
"Both Egypt and the United Kingdom are very disturbed by the lack of progress on the Middle East peace process.

"We recognise that this process cannot be taken for granted. It needs to be given a new dynamic, a new momentum," Britain's Foreign Secretary, Malcolm Rifkind, told reporters after talks with Egypt's Amre Moussa.
Rifkind said the first step to progress must be to implement a long-overdue deal for the redeployment of Israeli troops in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron.

He said the deterioration in confidence between Israelis and Palestinians was a cause for alarm and urged the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to make "further substantial progress" in boosting economic opportunities for Palestinians.

Moussa, who was in London for a Bosnian peace conference, said time was of the essence. But the Egyptian minister said that after meeting Netanyahu earlier in the week he still hoped the peace process could be kept alive.
"I still believe that the situation is retrievable, and I hope I'm right," Moussa said.
"We hope we all can help push forward and save the peace process. I entertain some hope in this direction and the situation, bad as it is, is still retrievable," he added.
